column2: On the authority of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Suckling makes unlawful what birth makes unlawful.” Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).
Al-raḍāʿah (“suckling”): nursing. “Makes unlawful what [birth] makes unlawful”: suckling makes unlawful the like of what birth makes unlawful.

Suckling is like lineage in making things unlawful, with regard to the prohibition of marriage and what follows from it, combining two sisters [in marriage] and the like, and treating them as relatives in permitting looking, being alone together and travelling together—but not in the other rulings, such as mutual inheritance, guardianship, maintenance and the like.
This hadith gives us a general, comprehensive principle for the rulings of suckling: what is unlawful through lineage is unlawful through suckling, whether on the wife's side or the husband's.
Every female relative by lineage whom a person is forbidden to marry, such as his sister, his maternal aunt and his paternal aunt,

it is likewise forbidden for him to marry if their relationship is by suckling. Likewise, a wife is forbidden to marry her son, brother, paternal uncle and maternal uncle, and so it is forbidden for her to marry these if they are [related to her] by suckling.
Some verse has been said on this:
The prohibition of suckling takes effect / as water flows through the veins.
